summary:
I wrote plan.md (no build or render yet). It lays the cathedral on the lidar massing: two flat-topped west towers (x 0..22, top y 98) with three deep portals, the Gallery of Kings, the west rose and the Grande Galerie; a steep lead roof over the nave and choir (ridge y 59), a transept with roses north and south (ridge y 57), and a socketed octagonal spire with apostle statues, its rooster tip at y 137.
The chevet is a half-cone apse ringed by ambulatories and five chapels, with one-block-thick flying buttresses and pinnacles on every pier. That outline, the cream sandstone against the dark deepslate lead and the warm dusk lighting make it read as Notre-Dame from the south-east camera. All blocks pass the 1.21.1 check. Exterior-only Gothic cathedral: cream sandstone masses, lead deepslate roofs, twin flat west towers with portals/kings/rose, chevet ringed by chapels with one-block flyers and pinnacles, octagonal dark spire (rooster y136, tip y137).
Six parts: shell, roofs, west front, chevet+flyers, spire, glass/light/grounds. Dusk lit with froglight floods, shroomlight behind glass, lanterns.

masonry shell: parts/shell.mjs builds the masonry shell: plinths to y3, towers with belfries, west front, nave, choir, transepts with gables, apse, rings, chapels, piers and sacristy. Openings are left as air. make.sh runs clean with no refused or off-palette writes, and the render reads as the right massing.
polish: The FOOTPRINT mask excludes x95..99 z0..4, so the north transept gable is clipped there. It also excludes x0..4 z5..9, which clips the north tower's NW corner.
Floating bits in the transept gables around the small rose: 10 cells at x93..97 y54..57 z69, 3 cells at x93..94 y54..55 z1. The roof part or P4 should tie them in.
A few orphan blocks from the polar chevet and chevet-pier rounding, about 8 cells near x156..175. P4 may need to tidy them.
Chevet piers y4..38 are built. P4 adds pinnacles on top (y39..44), the flyers and gargoyles.
Aisle and tribune lean-to roofs, flat chapel terraces and the apse cone are not built; they go to P2. The terrace slab at y21 is only a placeholder.
Windows and portals are carved only as voids. Glazing, the west front's carved detail, the y97..98 tower parapets and the buttress feet at x0..1 go to P3/P4/P6.
The axial chapel (r35) and the sacristy are simplified.
ashlarWall quoins were not used.

waste.what: Hand-coded the footprint mask as a lookup, the ground map, mirror about z37, and polar wall, window and pier clipping.
waste.cost: one large script, about 150 lines; one corrective pass for window voids in the band walls
waste.tool: vocab helpers that clip to the FOOTPRINT mask and ground by default (mask.json), plus a wall helper that takes a window list and a polar helper that returns mask-clipped cells

waste.what: Worked out west-front void layers (portal pointed profiles, kings' niches, rose disc, lancets) as predicate functions by hand
waste.cost: about 40 lines of coordinate logic
waste.tool: a 'solidWithVoids(box, voidList)' helper taking the reserved outlines from plan.md

waste.what: Checked the mask clipping and the floating gable cells only by reading check output and one render
waste.cost: 1 render, 1 check run
waste.tool: mcd check --site footprint mask reporting

companions.task: Quoins, string courses and set-offs on the towers, buttresses and piers
Exact footprint-mask clipping and a ground-height fit for every mass
Fill the window voids I left open in the bands and the apse

summary:
lead roofs: parts/roofs.mjs builds the lead roofs by hand with leadRoof: nave+choir gable (stops under the spire socle), transept gables, nave and choir aisle and tribune lean-tos, the apse half-cone, and the sacristy hall, wing and south chapel.
Eaves sit one course above each wall plate; make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes.
Ridges are at y55 instead of 59 (nave) and 57 (transepts) because leadRoof is pitch 1; the sacristy link roof, chevet ambulatory rings and chapel terraces are not built.
polish: Ridge heights: nave+choir ridge is y55 (plan 59) and transept ridges y55 (plan 57), because leadRoof is pitch 1; a steeper roof needs a pitch option.
Sacristy link gallery roof (x120..144, z70..84) not built.
Chevet ambulatory rings (r11..17 and r18..24) lean-to roofs not built.
Chapel terraces at y21 (nave and choir side chapels) not built.
Sacristy wing ridge is y19 (plan says 16), because the eave of 15 with pitch 1 gives that height.
Apse half-cone is a stepped solid stack of deepslate_tiles, not stairs-edged; chevet pinnacles and flyers are the chevet part's.
The sacristy lancets and door are the chevet/south part's, not this one.
The shell's orphan warnings (transept gable at x92..98 z1 and z69, and cells 156,44,29 and 156,44,45) are not from this part.

waste.what: Worked out each roof's box and eave by reading the shell's wall tops (y24, y33, y45) cell by cell, to keep the roofs off shell cells.
waste.cost: about 6 reads of shell.mjs and a few retries on the eave heights
waste.tool: A helper that takes the shell's wall tops from the shell part (or a wallTops(box) query) and returns each roof's eave, so eaves are never guessed.

waste.what: Hand-wrote the apse half-cone as a per-column loop over polar cells instead of a shape brush.
waste.cost: one loop of about 40 lines, plus a stepped (not stairs) surface
waste.tool: A cone/half-revolve brush in the build library (the shapes-curved helpers) that lays a stair-edged conical roof with a given pitch and footprint.

waste.what: Had no way to vary pitch on leadRoof, so the ridges come out at 55 instead of the plan's 59 and 57.
waste.cost: not fixed; a second gable course would have been needed
waste.tool: leadRoof with a pitch option (1.4 as the plan asks), or the roof tool's --spec with pitch 1.4 and footprint boxes, which would reach the plan heights.

companions.task: Lay the lead on the nave, choir and transept slopes at a steeper pitch with proper lead-sheet seams and the ridge crest; take the chevet ambulatory rings and the sacristy link gallery roof, which I did not build.
Frame the nave and choir gable at pitch 1.4 so the ridge reaches y59, and carry the hidden timber under the lead.
Cut the eave course and parapet gutters where the lean-tos meet the clerestory and tribune walls, so the lead runs clean over the wall tops.

summary:
west front: parts/west.mjs builds the west front: three pointed portals (doorways open at y 4, doors at the back), 28 Gallery of Kings niches, the west rose frame and tracery (glass left for P6), tower lancet pairs and belfry lancets with blue glass, the Grande Galerie colonnade, the Virgin's-gallery and terrace balustrades, and facade buttress set-offs.
make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt: the west front placed 3845 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. Its own floating blocks are gone; the remaining floating groups are in the transept gables (not this part).
Not built: tower cornices, decks and corner pinnacles, belfry louvres, chimeras at y 68, portal tympana (vocab portal() fills the splay with chiseled and openPortal() clears it, so the tympana are lost), and the rose glass (P6).
polish: Tower cornices (y 95), decks and corner pinnacles to y 98, and the belfry louvres (dark_oak_trapdoor) are not placed; the tower tops are still the shell's.

Portal tympana and lintel carving are lost: vocab portal() fills the splay with chiseled_sandstone, so openPortal() in west.mjs clears the whole void. The doorways read open but the carved tympanum is missing.
Chimeras (gargoyle stairs +2) at the tower corners y 68 are not placed.
West rose glass is left open for P6 (glazeOpening). The lancets already carry blue glass with purple heads from lancetOpening, so P6 must not double-place them.

mcd fit reports 6 cells 'stairs on a bottom slab' from helper output: the lancet arch stairs over the sill slab at (0,72,8/13/21/26) and the set-off stairs at (2,43,9) and (2,43,65). Fix in the vocab helpers (sill or set-off slab level), not by hand.

Plan.md has no checklist; I ticked the 3 matching elements.md items (facade buttresses, portals, Gallery of Kings) and added a Notes line on the portal sill (y 4, the rock top under the towers is y 3) and the openPortal workaround.

waste.what: Portal void: vocab portal() fills the splay with chiseled_sandstone, so I had to write openPortal() to clear it cell by cell, then probe the grid with a throwaway script to find it.
waste.cost: about 3 build-and-probe rounds, roughly 40 cell checks by script
waste.tool: portal() needs an { open: true } option (or a tympanum-only fill) so a doorway comes out as a void without a local carve pass.

waste.what: Checking the portal and belfry geometry: I rendered zoom tiles and read the block layout at each y with an ad-hoc probe, since the front elevation at 300px hides the openings.
waste.cost: 3 zoom renders and 2 probe scripts
waste.tool: mcd zoom with a --cells or --probe option printing the block at a list of coordinates, plus a helper that dumps one x-z slice of the grid as text.

waste.what: Sill and arch stair mismatch: lancetOpening's arch stairs and setoffButtress's set-off stairs sit over bottom slabs with air under them, and I found them only by reading mcd fit output cell by cell.
waste.cost: one fit run, 6 cells listed by hand
waste.tool: A fit-aware lancetOpening option (sill as a top slab, or stairs placed one course up), so the helper never emits a stair over a bottom slab.

waste.what: Floating colonnade ends: I shortened the colonnade line by trial (z 7..67 floated, z 9..65 holds) after a check run, rather than knowing the tower's face cells in advance.
waste.cost: 2 make.sh and check cycles
waste.tool: A coordinate dump of the shell's solid cells along a face (the masonry shell's occupancy on x 0..3) so a line can be sized before placing.

companions.task: Fit the west rose glass (blue field, red ring, purple and yellow centre) and check the lancet glass against the openings, so P6 glazes what is open and nothing is double-placed.
Carve the three portal tympana (chiseled and cut lintel, with the Last Judgement, Virgin and St Anne reliefs) and the tower cornices and corner pinnacles, which the vocab helpers can't carve.
Hang the belfry louvres (open dark_oak_trapdoor pairs) inside each belfry lancet so the bells show from below, and set the shutters on the tower decks.

summary:
chevet, south side and flyers: P4 chevet part (parts/chevet.mjs) built: nave and choir flyers on both sides (z 66→48, z 8→26), six radial chevet flyers, pinnacles on every pier top, chevet gargoyles at y 36.
Transept gables get north and south roses (centre x 95, y 34, r 7), portals, and apex pinnacles; an apse-eave sandstone_wall ring sits at y 46.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt (chevet part: 3444 placed, 22 refused where flyer stairs meet shell piers and walls, 0 off-palette).
polish: Ring windows and chapel lancets (chevet ring walls, choir and nave clerestory and aisles) are not built; they are shell cells and need the glazier.
Nave and choir gargoyles are not built: the outward cells on the north and south faces fall outside the footprint mask.
Transept gable gallery (y 43..45), the gable triangle small rose (r 2 at y 51) and the apex-pinnacle base at y 57 are not built or float until the lead-roofs part lays the ridge.
22 flyer stairs were refused where the radial and pier flyers meet shell piers and walls; the flyers have small gaps at those joints.
The elements.md CHEVET item and the transept item stay unticked, because they cover parts this module does not build.
The gable apex pinnacles (x 95, z 68 and z 2, y 57..60) float in the current check until the roofs part adds the ridge.

waste.what: Radial chevet flyers: vocab flyer() only spans along x or z, so I hand-rolled a radial stepper (r 30→11, quarter-sine rise) with rounding and dedupe.
waste.cost: one helper, about 40 lines, plus one refusal-and-retry pass
waste.tool: flyer() taking a from/to pair in any horizontal direction (radial or diagonal), or a polar variant of flyer() like ringWall's arc.

waste.what: Gargoyle and pinnacle placement checked against the footprint mask by hand: many candidate cells fall outside the 5x5 mask (nave and choir piers at the north and south faces), so I dropped them.
waste.cost: about 10 mask lookups worked out cell by cell, then the nave/choir gargoyles were abandoned
waste.tool: A mask-aware placement helper (inMask(x,z) exported from the shell) that the vocab helpers call, returning which cells of a planned element fall outside the footprint before writing.

waste.what: Apse-eave balustrade: the apse is round, and balustrade() only takes straight lines, so I looped over angles and rounded the cells by hand.
waste.cost: one loop, a few retries on the radius rounding
waste.tool: balustrade() accepting an arc (centre, radius, angle range) as well as a straight line.

waste.what: Checking the build: I looked at the back-elevation render and read the refusal and floating lists by eye rather than checking the flyers against the clerestory and pier cells with a tool.
waste.cost: two render reads, one structure check
waste.tool: A per-part report that lists each element's cells as built, refused, or floating, so a flyer's end-to-wall contact can be verified without rendering.

companions.task: Ring windows and chapel lancets in the chevet and choir walls, and the gargoyles on the nave and choir piers, which sit outside the footprint on the north and south faces and need a shifted placement.
The transept rose glass and the small gable roses (r 2) with the purple and red pane rings, so the roses read through the gable masonry.
The transept gable apex, which the apex pinnacles at y 57 stand on, and the lead ridge joining the gable and the roofs, so the pinnacles stop floating.
The six radial chevet flyers: the upside-down soffit and the upright coping, and the joints where each flyer meets its pier top and the apse wall.

summary:
spire: parts/spire.mjs builds the octagonal lead spire at x95 z37: socle y52..60, lower open stage y61..76 with eight louvred lancets and eight pinnacles to y80, needle y77..132 with crockets at 84/98/112/124, cross and rooster, and the lightning-rod tip at (95,137,37).
Twelve apostle statues stand on the crossing ridges (feet y60 west/east, y58 north/south).
make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt: spire 2044 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; the zoomed renders read as a spire.
polish: The socle base (y52) and the north/south apostles (feet y58) float in `mcd check` until the lead roofs part fills the crossing under y52 and the transept/nave ridges (y57/59); not a spire fault, a dependency on parts/roofs.mjs.
Lower stage lancets are plain openings with trapdoor louvres; no gabled heads at the top of each lancet.
Eight corner pinnacles are plain polished_deepslate_wall columns to y80 with no cap; the pale tone in the render is the renderer's approximation of the wall, not a palette fault.
The six-block crocket rings use the spireStage default crocket width; not checked against the plan's crocket 'one cell wider' wording beyond the render.

waste.what: Hand-wrote a local octagon outline and vertex-log logic in spire.mjs because spireStage/octagonRing cannot omit the eight lancet cells of the lower open stage.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of local helpers, one extra pass to confirm the outline matches octagonRing
waste.tool: octagonRing / spireStage option `openings: [[dx,dz,y0,y1]]` (recess by omission per face centre) plus `louvres` so the lancet stage is one call

waste.what: Placed the cross, rooster and tip cell by cell with a put-if-air wrapper.
waste.cost: 6 writes, one retry on the iron_chain trap (B.chain defaults to iron_chain, needed version26=false)
waste.tool: a `column(g, x, y0, y1, z, [...])` or a spire `cross()` helper, and a note in the vocab that B.chain defaults to iron_chain

waste.what: Checked the spire's floating blocks and statues by reading `$MCD check` output by eye, to separate the expected crossing-roof dependency from a real fault.
waste.cost: one check run and a judgement call
waste.tool: `$MCD check` could tag floating groups that rest on another part's cells, so a part's dependencies are visible

companions.task: Lay the lead cladding and the crossing-roof fill under the socle (y52) so the spire stops floating, and take the ridge seams where the apostles stand.
Carve the apostle heads and the pinnacle crockets so they read as statues and not stacked stair blocks at a distance.
Make the iron_bars cross arms and the cresting, and fix the chain and gold rooster at the tip.

summary:
glass, light and grounds: P6 (parts/finish.mjs) glazes the nave, choir, tribune, chapel and apse openings, the transept and west roses, and the tower lancet pairs in blue panes with purple heads. It also paves z70..73 and plants the Square Jean-XXIII garden (grass, moss, azalea) with 4 lamp posts and 2 floodlights.
Make.sh runs clean: the glass part placed 2665 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette, and `mcd check` reports 0 floating blocks. The render shows the glazing reading on the clerestory and rose windows.
Not done: shroomlight behind the glass (it floats in the void), pier-foot floodlights (z70 is outside the footprint), and lamp posts on the west parvis and north side (no ground there in the plot).
polish: Shroomlight behind the roses floats in the void and fails the structure check; it needs a shell-side support (a cut_sandstone ledge or a chain from a beam) before it can go in.

Dusk light is only partial: 2 ochre_froglight floods and 4 lamp posts in the garden. The plan's pier-foot floodlights are not placed, because z 70 under the nave piers is outside the footprint mask, and the west parvis is outside the plot.
Ambulatory r18..24 windows are not glazed (plan gives no window spec for them).
Sacristy lancets and the belfry louvres are not glazed here (P4 and P3 own them). Glass for the sacristy lancets still needs doing.
Plan.md checklist is not in the file I read, so I only ticked the Grounds item in elements.md; the glass and light items stay open because they are partial.
The shell's orphan blocks (93,54,1 and similar, 3 left after my rebuild) are not from this part and are left for the shell owner.

waste.what: Worked out each glazed box by hand: nave, choir and tribune bay centres from the pier pairs, the chapel and clerestory x ranges, and the tower lancet z ranges.
waste.cost: About 40 coordinate boxes typed by hand across 6 loops, plus two retries when I confused the glass plane with the wall plane.
waste.tool: A bay-rhythm helper such as `bays(piers, width)` that returns the bay centres from plan.md's pier table, and an opening table keyed by name so a glazing part reads it directly.

waste.what: Curved apse and chevet ring windows: I wrote the tangent-offset trig for each cell myself (`ringWindow`).
waste.cost: One helper, about 12 lines, plus one rebuild to correct the head-row offset.
waste.tool: A vocab helper `ringWindow(cx, cz, r, angle, y0, y1, headRows)` for polar window placement, matching ringWall's bays.

waste.what: Checked by trial whether a floodlight or shroomlight sits on a footprint cell and has support, by rebuilding and reading the check output.
waste.cost: Three full make.sh rebuilds (about 20 s each) to find the floating shroomlights and the footprint limit.
waste.tool: `mcd check` run on a single part before the full build, or a footprint-mask query (`isInside(x,z)`) in the build library so a part can test its cells first.

waste.what: Glazing and ring windows pane connections are set with hand-written state dictionaries.
waste.cost: Dozens of state objects; the apse panes all carry the same all-false connections.
waste.tool: A pane helper that derives the north/south/east/west connections from the neighbours already placed (the `glazeOpening` code does this for straight runs but not for curves).

companions.task: Lay out the rose tracery and the apse lancets' pane joints, and decide which curved windows need a purple head row rather than a full blue field.
Place the pier-foot floodlights and lamp posts where the plan wants them, and sort out which of them the footprint and the ground allow.
Extend the Square Jean-XXIII planting (trees, azaleas, a proper path to the sacristy link) and give the paving its garden edge.

summary: inspection: Fixed the 8 listed fit issues by changing the lancet sill in the shared vocab helper from a bottom slab to a top slab, so the upside-down arch stairs no longer float over air. make.sh rebuilt build.nbt; walk is ok (14211 cells reached, no rooms unreachable) and fit reports OK.

waste.what: Traced each listed cell back to its source by hand: the eight cells are arch-end stairs of lancets (x 0 belfry lancets at z 8/13/21/26/48/53, x 2 rose-stage lancets at y 43 z 9/65), worked out from lancet widths and sill extents.
waste.cost: About 6 coordinate calculations and 3 file reads before the cause was clear.
waste.tool: mcd fit should name the source helper or part for each cell (e.g. 'lancetOpening sill at y 71') so the fix location is one lookup.

waste.what: The fit output printed 8 issue lines but its header said 12 issues; the other 4 were not listed, so I could not confirm them by name. I rebuilt and reran fit, which now reports OK.
waste.cost: One extra rebuild and fit run.
waste.tool: mcd fit should print all issues, or state the omitted count and where to find them, not just a truncated head.
